title: XRPL x402 and MPP payment rails, RLUSD chain split, Mastercard ecosystem links and transaction-value reconciliation

research_window.note: Sources were inspected through rendered publisher pages. Original response bytes, HTTP headers and independent timestamp anchors were not retained.

append_only.purpose: Preserve first-party XRPL x402/MPP technical details, Mastercard ecosystem participation, third-party on-chain RLUSD chain supply and cross-publisher agent-payment metric disagreement without treating transaction counts as capital flows.

source_capture_policy.reason: Evidence is rendered web material and self-reported network metrics. The payment statistics lack a byte-complete raw transaction ledger extract, exact source cutoffs and an independent reconciliation of value by asset. These are institutional/payment-rail context, not a calibrated XRP price feature.

stated_method: XRPL rippled gateway_balances on RLUSD issuer address
Cross-check against rl-tracker.com; publisher states match within less than $1M
limitations: The rendered page does not expose exact per-chain block/ledger indexes or raw JSON receipts.
Displayed values are rounded; displayed XRPL and Ethereum amounts do not sum exactly to the rounded total.
Base, Optimism, Ink, Unichain and XRPL EVM sidechain have small supplies excluded from the two-chain total.
The publisher's page is an aggregator, not the issuer's own reserve attestation.
Transaction count, value, merchant and service metrics are publisher-reported; no complete raw ledger transaction export was captured.

The visible live-settlement list contains entries labelled 'Unverified' even though the product describes verification before settlement; displayed live entries must not all be treated as verified settlements.
The page does not expose a full asset-by-asset all-time USD reconciliation.
The dashboard metrics may have different refresh times and inclusion rules from third-party XRP Radar.
Documentation describes intended implementation and validation logic; it does not independently prove every production transaction passed each control.
No paid service was called and no payment transaction was submitted during this research.
This is a product/developer announcement, not independent evidence of customer production volume.
Beta SDK and payment-channel functionality must not be described as broad commercial adoption.
The partner list establishes participation/support for Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines, not a direct commercial contract between every listed company.
The release does not disclose XRP-specific settlement volume, XRP purchases or market liquidity.
MPP is an open protocol; its existence does not establish any specific XRPL customer or transaction volume.
The article cites a Ripple release shared with CoinDesk and t54 dashboard figures; those figures are not independent ledger-wide measurements.
The 1 XRP account reserve is a protocol account-activation requirement, not evidence that every new account bought XRP on an exchange.
No complete commercial usage or revenue breakdown for the Privy integration is disclosed.

rlusd_chain_supply.other_network_supply_description: Small supply; exact amounts not included in the two-chain figure.
rlusd_chain_supply.interpretation: The displayed supply is multi-chain and majority Ethereum. The two-chain total is not all-chain RLUSD supply and is not XRP collateral or XRP demand.

vintage_comparison.interpretation: The $27M difference is not treated as a contradiction: the dates differ, and XRP Insights explicitly excludes small supplies on other networks from its XRPL+Ethereum total.

supported_assets: XRPL issued assets such as RLUSD
x402.payment_flow: Seller returns HTTP 402 payment requirements; payer signs a standard XRPL Payment; facilitator submits the signed transaction; the payer pays the XRPL transaction fee.
security_controls: Payer-signed transaction; facilitator does not need the payer's raw private key.
Destination and amount must match the advertised requirements.
RLUSD issued-asset payment requires canonical currency code and issuer address.
Invoice binding is mandatory through MemoData equal to invoice ID or InvoiceID equal to SHA-256(invoice ID).
LastLedgerSequence is required for bounded expiry.
Fee limits, no partial payments and no cross-currency payments.
Invoices are consumed once settlement succeeds to enforce idempotency.
x402.limitation: These are documented protocol controls, not an independent audit of all production transactions.

machine_payments_protocol.stablecoin_session_support: Pending XRPL IOU/MPT Payment Channel support tracked as XLS-93d.
machine_payments_protocol.description: MPP is distinct from x402. RippleX reports XRPL settlement support for MPP single charges and XRP Payment Channel sessions; RLUSD session payments are not yet described as live.

open_wallet_standard.ripplex_integration: XRPL supported in RippleX AI Starter Kit v1.1 through a policy-gated OWS signing interface.
open_wallet_standard.key_handling_claim: Local-first encrypted vault; keys decrypted only long enough to sign and wiped from memory; agent requests policy-gated signatures rather than handling raw private keys.
open_wallet_standard.relationship_classification: Technical ecosystem overlap only. This does not establish a direct Circle-Ripple corporate partnership, Circle use of XRPL, or USDC payment volume on XRPL.

t54_first_party_dashboard.visible_live_list_status: Several visible entries are labelled Unverified.
t54_first_party_dashboard.interpretation: The displayed count is high, but the displayed lifetime dollar value is small. The implied average is a rough ratio of two publisher dashboard totals, not an audited per-transaction average.

coindesk_oct14_report.additional_reported_integration: Ripple/Stripe-owned Privy embedded XRPL wallets for XRP, RLUSD and other network assets.

cross_source_disagreement.interpretation: Counts, merchant/service definitions and value vintages differ. The known XRP+RLUSD value from XRP Radar does not exactly reconcile to t54's USD dashboard total; other assets, pricing conventions or snapshot windows may explain the difference, but no explanation is assumed.

limitations: Transaction count is not dollar volume, unique users, revenue, net capital inflow or XRP buy pressure.
A large share of activity is sub-cent per-request micropayment activity.
The t54 hub and XRP Radar display different transaction counts and service/agent counts.
The XRP Radar page cites on-chain verification and one recent sample ledger/transaction, but no complete raw transaction export was captured.
No per-asset daily volume or market-purchase breakdown was disclosed.

mastercard_agent_pay_for_machines.function: Credentialing, permissioning and orchestration for agent/machine payments across cards, accounts and stablecoins.
mastercard_agent_pay_for_machines.relationship_classification: Shared Mastercard ecosystem participation; not proof of a direct Coinbase-Ripple or Coinbase-t54 commercial agreement, and not proof of XRP settlement volume.

stripe_tempo_mpp.relationship: Stripe and Tempo co-authored the Machine Payments Protocol; RippleX later announced XRPL as a supported settlement rail.
stripe_tempo_mpp.relationship_classification: Protocol integration and ecosystem interoperability; not evidence of a Stripe-Ripple capital investment or commercial payment volume.

circle_ows.relationship: RippleX says Circle is among the contributors to the Open Wallet Standard that RippleX integrated for XRPL wallet access.
circle_ows.relationship_classification: Technical standards overlap only; no direct Circle-Ripple corporate partnership, USDC-on-XRPL usage or capital flow established.

privy_stripe_ripple.relationship: CoinDesk reported Ripple integrating Stripe-owned Privy wallet infrastructure into XRPL applications for embedded XRP/RLUSD wallets.
privy_stripe_ripple.relationship_classification: Product/wallet integration reported by CoinDesk; commercial usage and XRP purchase volume not disclosed.

sbi.relationship: No SBI/SBI Holdings/SBIC role was established in the specific Mastercard AP4M, RippleX MPP or t54 x402 sources reviewed in this artifact.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: Agentic payment activity may create many XRPL transactions without representing large capital flows.
supporting_evidence: t54 reports 15.196M transactions and $63,129.67 all-time settled value.
The implied average from those dashboard totals is approximately $0.00415 per transaction.
disconfirming_or_missing: Publisher metrics have not been independently reconciled to a complete raw ledger transaction set.
The value may omit or use different pricing conventions for some assets.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: RLUSD adoption is not predominantly on XRPL by supply; Ethereum holds the majority in the captured two-chain view.
supporting_evidence: XRP Insights reports 871.1M USD on XRPL (34%) and 1.73B USD on Ethereum (66%).
disconfirming_or_missing: Other networks have small supplies excluded from the two-chain total.
Exact block/ledger receipts were not captured.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: x402 currently supports XRP and RLUSD single payments, while MPP's XRP Payment Channel session mode does not yet support stablecoin sessions.
supporting_evidence: t54 x402 documentation supports XRP and issued assets such as RLUSD.
RippleX says MPP single charges support XRP, IOU and MPT, while Payment Channel sessions currently use XRP and stablecoin support is pending XLS-93d.
disconfirming_or_missing: No production customer volume or adoption split by protocol/asset was disclosed.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: Coinbase, Ripple/RippleX, t54, Stripe and Tempo participate in the same Mastercard agent-payment ecosystem, while Circle has a separate OWS technical overlap.
supporting_evidence: Mastercard's June 10 release names Coinbase, Ripple, RippleX, t54 Labs, Stripe and Tempo among initial participants/supporters.
RippleX names Circle among OWS contributors.
disconfirming_or_missing: Mastercard's partner list does not disclose specific bilateral agreements or XRP settlement.
RippleX's OWS mention does not establish a Circle-Ripple commercial partnership.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: The 1 XRP reserve needed to activate a new XRPL account can create protocol-level XRP lock-up but does not prove an open-market XRP purchase.
supporting_evidence: CoinDesk reports each new XRPL account must receive a 1 XRP reserve, even if used only for stablecoin payments.
disconfirming_or_missing: The XRP may already be held by the user, supplied by a wallet provider or recycled from an existing reserve; no market source is established.

reasons: No byte-complete raw source payloads, transaction exports or SHA-256 receipts were captured.
Exact source retrieval timestamps and independent timestamp anchors are absent.
t54 and XRP Radar display different transaction counts and value vintages.
The payment dashboard's average value per transaction is a rough ratio, not an audited unit-economics measure.
RLUSD chain supply is not XRP supply or XRP collateral.
Payment-rail participation and protocol support do not establish market purchases or XRP price impact.
No evaluator-attested out-of-sample predictive lift, probability calibration or shadow outcome is connected to these observations.

next_actions: Capture XRPL ledger indexes and raw rippled gateway_balances for the RLUSD issuer, plus Ethereum contract totalSupply() receipts and transaction hashes.

Collect a complete t54 x402 transaction export with transaction hash, ledger index, asset, amount, issuer, destination, SourceTag, invoice binding and settlement status; reconcile every sample against rippled.
Separate XRP, RLUSD and USDC transaction counts and USD values by day; distinguish pending, unverified, failed and settled payments.
Verify Mastercard AP4M participation scope for each listed company and identify specific product integrations before drawing bilateral relationship edges.
Track XLS-93d amendment status from official XRPL sources before describing RLUSD Payment Channel sessions as live.
Keep all payment-rail metrics out of XRP price features until raw receipts, point-in-time availability and independent reconciliation are established.
Do not invoke paid x402 services or submit any payment without separate explicit authorization.
